## Introduction {#sec-introduction}

*"Sana all"*^[literal translation: hope all] is a popular Taglish^[mixture of Tagalog and English] slang among Filipinos. The closest English equivalent would be "must be nice", except the speaker wishes the experience for everyone. This is exactly how I feel whenever I come across government websites from other countries, usually from the developed ones, that are equipped with multiple ways to access public data.

*Sana all may API.* (It must be nice if every government, particularly mine, provides an API for accessing public data.)

While the Philippine government has implemented several open data initiatives, including the passage of the Freedom of Information Act and OpenGov partnership, it still has a long way to go in publishing data that are catered for analysts. For instance, although the Department of Budget and Management (DBM) has posted [budget document archives](https://www.dbm.gov.ph/index.php/budget-documents-archives) dating back to 1980s, it is incomplete, with multiple years missing. Additionally, many documents are provided as scanned PDFs, which are challenging to work with.

As I write this, I found an [open-source API for budget documents](https://github.com/bettergovph/open-budget-api) developed by a [group of Filipino engineers and volunteers](https://bettergov.ph/about) who share the sentiment as mine. However, I will not be using this API. Instead, my goal for this project is to build a tidy dataset straight from the source.

## Downloading the data {#sec-downloading-the-data}

The budget documents I am looking for are the National Expenditure Program (NEP) and General Appropriations Act (GAA). These documents live in the [DBM website](https://www.dbm.gov.ph) under the budget tab.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code  code-fold="false"}
page_home <- "https://www.dbm.gov.ph"
page_budget <- paste(page_home, "index.php", "budget", sep = "/")
```
:::


Using the rvest package, Let's retrieve the contents of `page_budget`


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
library(rvest)
```
:::


Here, I created a function that retrieves all hyperlinks from a specified web page and filters them based on a matching pattern.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
#' Extract and Filter Links from a Web Page
#'
#' This function retrieves all hyperlinks from a specified web page and filters them based on a matching pattern.
#'
#' @param page A character string representing the URL of the webpage to scrape. 
#' @param pattern A regular expression pattern to filter the links.
#' @param delay A numeric value indicating seconds to wait before fetching the page. Default is 2 seconds.
#'
#' @return A character vector containing all links that match the specified pattern.
#' @export
#'
#' @examples
#' # get_links("https://example.com", "pattern")
get_links <- function(page, pattern, delay = 2) {
  # Validate input parameters
  if (!is.character(page) || length(page) != 1) {
    stop("Invalid URL input. Please provide a single character string URL.")
  }
  
  if (!is.character(pattern) || length(pattern) != 1) {
    stop("Invalid pattern input. Please provide a single character string pattern.")
  }

  if (!is.numeric(delay) || delay < 0) {
    stop("Delay must be a non-negative numeric value.")
  }
  
  Sys.sleep(delay)  # Pause execution to avoid overwhelming the server
  
  # Extract links
  links <- page |>
    read_html() |> 
    html_elements("a") |> 
    html_attr("href") 

  # Filter links using the specified pattern
  filtered_links <- grepv(pattern = pattern, x = links)

  return(filtered_links)
}
```
:::



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code  code-fold="false"}
pattern <- "\\d{4}/(general-appropriations-act|national-expenditure-program)"

links_budget <- get_links(page_budget, pattern)
```
:::
